items.text: Mainstream media really needs to stop with these sensationalized, conflated FUD headlines. I get it, you want to generate clicks. But you’re misleading your audience. FT headline: "Nvidia behind $50 billion lease on Texas data centre that will use its chips" Over 30 years after renewals? Reality: "Nvidia’s 15-year lease commitment for the Texas site is worth $19.6bn, and renewal options would take the total value to $50bn over 30 years, according to Hut 8."

items.text: JIM CRAMER SAYS NVIDIA'S POTENTIAL $250 BILLION BACKSTOP FOR OPENAI HAS HIM THINKING ABOUT 2000. Jim said the story that Nvidia $NVDA is in talks to guarantee $250 billion in financing for OpenAI's Ohio data center project Cramer said the arrangement reminds him of dot-com era telecom equipment makers who financed their own customers' purchases. "I lived through 2000. I don't want the sequel." Cramer's actual concern isn't NVIDIA's balance sheet: "What we learned in 2000 is that you don't lend to companies who buy your goods." He was explicit that he isn't predicting a crash, and still views NVIDIA as an exceptionally strong company. The distinction he draws is about who ends up holding the risk if a customer can't pay: "If the buyer, in this case, OpenAI, can actually afford to pay for these chips, perhaps because it comes public, then NVIDIA's in terrific shape. If the buyer can't pay, well, that's a different story." "NVIDIA shouldn't make these guarantees even if it has all the money in the world. Just history, that's all, just history."

items.text: We tested Nemotron 3 Ultra on agentic chip design. The task is RTL coding: a model iteratively writes the code that defines a chip's logic, runs it through a simulator, reads the failures, and rewrites. Across nine categories of real design work, Nemotron 3 Ultra averaged a 97.1% pass rate at 6,629 tokens per iteration, best of the open models tested on both.
